speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing those episodes of unresponsiveness with facial grimacing. To better understand what's happening, could you tell me if these events ever happen while you are asleep, or if they occur only when you are awake?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cataplexy secondary to Narcolepsy Type 1 (with atypical semiology) OR Absence Status/Complex Partial Seizure. Given the "muddy taste" and post-ictal confusion, this strongly suggests a seizure disorder rather than cataplexy. I need to rule out structural causes.

REQUEST TEST: EEG (Electroencephalogram)
REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI
REQUEST IMAGES: Please show me an EEG report or brain MRI if available.
